To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mutations that affect amino acids common to SV40 T and t antigens result in a mutant virus that is defective for productive viral replication, viral assembly and release, and transformation.

mutations of the host range- and adenovirus helper functions of SV40 T antigen inactivate a function required for viral DNA replication, while mutations of a region of T antigen common to the large (T) and small (t) antigens inactivate a function that is required subsequent for DNA replication, such as viral assembly and release.

the mutations in the host-range adenovirus helper function of SV40 T antigen inactivate a function required for viral maturation, and that the same mutations inactivate a second function required for cell transformation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of viral replication and transformation and the role of DNA tumor viruses in cancer.
the identification of the functions of T antigen and the viral genes required for productive SV40 infection.
the characterization of the DNA replication-positive, transformation-defective mutant of SV40, 5002.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the mutations in the 5002 mutant of SV40 affect the T antigen function(s) that are required for viral maturation, assembly and/or release, but not those required for DNA replication, and that these mutations also affect a function(s) that is required for transformation of REF51 cells.
the mutations in the T/t antigen region of 5002 inactivate an essential activity of this protein, which is required for productive infection but not for DNA replication.
the 5002 mutant is defective in the T antigen functions of viral assembly and/or release of virions, as well as transformation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

T antigen encodes a number of different activities, including DNA replication, transformation, and viral maturation, that are all required for productive viral infection and that the host range-Ad helper function of T antigen is not required for transformation.

the mutations in the host-range-adenovirus-helper function domain affect the ability of T antigen to transform cells, while mutations in the 5002 domain affect the ability to produce infectious virions.
the 5002 mutant is defective in the production of infectious virus and transformation, but is capable of replicative DNA synthesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

T antigen has two distinct functions in SV40 infection: (i) a function required for viral DNA replication that is encoded by the host range- adenovirus helper function domain and (ii) a second function required for viral assembly, release, and/or transformation that is encoded by a different region of the T antigen protein.
the mutations in 5002 alter the activity of T antigen in a way that is specific for transformation and productive infection, but not for DNA replication.
T antigen is capable of multiple functions that affect viral infection and cellular transformation.
